01 / THE POINT

Less digital. More analogue.

Technology isn’t the enemy. It just doesn’t get the best seat for a week.

We don’t offer answers. We create an environment where you might find your own direction through doing, talking, listening, and living alongside other people.

02 / THE WEEK

Seven-day field log

A rhythm, not a packed schedule.

There is time to learn something useful—and time to do absolutely nothing.

  1. 07:30

    Wake slowly

    Breakfast. Coffee. Weather. No morning scroll required.

    begin here
  2. 09:30

    Use your hands—or your head

    A practical workshop, a debate, or both. Learn from mentors, moderators, locals, and one another.

  3. 13:00

    Make lunch together

    Planning, chopping, cooking, eating, cleaning. Everyone contributes to life at camp.

  5. 15:08

    Nothing is scheduled

    Read. Sleep. Walk. Play cards. Help in the garden. Have a ridiculous conversation—or an important one.

  6. 19:24

    Fire, food, stories

    Dinner, games, music, stars. Tomorrow can wait until tomorrow.

Learn by doing.
Think by talking.

OUR ROLE: CREATE THE ENVIRONMENT / NOT DICTATE THE ANSWER

04 / THE MOUNTAIN NIGHT

Leave from camp. On foot.

Carry what you need.
Sleep under the stars.
Walk home different.

One night in the mountains, reached under your own power. A real challenge with experienced leadership, thoughtful planning, and proper equipment—not survival training.

05 / MEMORY

Phones down. Cameras up.

Capture it.
Don’t post it.

Smartphones are stored safely and remain available when needed. There are designated times to contact home, and the camp can always be reached in an emergency.

Instead, take a digital camera. Photograph the week. Bring the memory card home.

keep this one →
06 / THE PLACE

A real village. Not a resort.

Rooted in the place—and the people already there.

An old house or simple base. A garden. Tents. The everyday life of a mountain community.

Local people and craftspeople may share food, agriculture, woodworking, music, culture, and knowledge accumulated over generations. The village is part of the relationship, not scenery.

SAFETY NOTE / 001

The experience includes hiking, outdoor living, and intentional discomfort. Appropriate equipment, planning, and experienced leadership are fundamental. Full eligibility, accessibility, and safety details will come with pilot registration.

08 / ASK US

Useful questions

Before you pack.

Do I have to give up my phone completely?+

No. Phones are stored safely for most of the experience and remain available when needed. The point is distance, not punishment.

Can my family reach me?+

Yes. There will be designated opportunities to contact home, and the camp remains reachable in an emergency.

Do I need hiking or camping experience?+

The pilot is designed around learning by doing, but final experience and fitness requirements will be shared before applications open.

What equipment is provided?+

Proper hiking backpacks, reliable tents, and sleeping bags suitable for temperatures around 0°C are planned. A final packing list will accompany registration.

Is this survival training?+

No. There is challenge and manageable discomfort, balanced by experienced leadership, planning, and suitable equipment.

Who leads the workshops and expedition?+

Practical mentors, knowledgeable guests, moderators, and experienced outdoor leadership will shape the program. Names and credentials will be published with the pilot details.

When is it, and how much will it cost?+

Dates and pricing are not set yet. Join the pilot list and we’ll share them when the first week is ready.
